items.description: TSV diagnostics and unchecked dependency names can contain control characters.
items.evidence: _report_timestamp and change-state diagnostics include paths and error details; the change-status schema currently requires dependency values only to be non-empty strings.
items.analysis: Even when invalid names are excluded and status and kind are constrained by enums, diagnostics may include dynamic filesystem or error data. Dependency entries are change names and must meet the same validity rules; the current schema and reader do not yet enforce those rules.
items.recommendation: For TSV change-list diagnostics, present only a static reason describing the cause, without paths, offending values, or other dynamic data. Validate dependency entries using the change-name rules without requiring the named change to exist.
items.rationale: Diagnostics should communicate only a static cause; dependency entries are change names and are subject to the same name-validity rules.

items.description: Index regeneration can follow a symlinked skill directory outside the target.
items.evidence: _regenerate_index writes through the installed specle directory without a containment check.
items.analysis: A symlink can redirect the generated index outside the requested target; the thread is outdated but the current path still follows it.
items.recommendation: Reject redirected index paths or verify containment before writing.
items.rationale: The target installation is user-controlled; users are responsible for their own symlinks and resulting changes to their Specle installation.

items.description: Invalid change names can inject terminal controls or spreadsheet formulas into reports.
items.evidence: Invalid directory names are emitted unchanged in text and CSV rows.
items.analysis: Rejected directory names are currently converted into synthetic change rows, despite not representing changes.
items.recommendation: Exclude invalidly named directories from change rows rather than escaping synthetic rows.
items.rationale: A rejected directory name is not a change and must not be presented as a synthetic change row.

items.description: Index regeneration rejects inventories with lifecycle diagnostics.
items.evidence: _regenerate_index checks inventory.lifecycle.diagnostics before generating the index.
items.analysis: Lifecycle diagnostics may indicate an incomplete or inconsistent managed inventory, so the default should preserve the index and explain the problem.
items.recommendation: Report lifecycle diagnostics and refuse index regeneration by default; add an index --force option that reports the diagnostics and permits regeneration despite them. Retain the separate valid managed specle skill requirement.
items.rationale: An incomplete or inconsistent index should be blocked with an explanation by default; --force may override lifecycle diagnostics, which must still be displayed.

items.description: Collection and selector diagnostics are omitted from changes reports.
items.evidence: _report_changes renders records and per-record issues but not snapshot.diagnostics.
items.analysis: The thread is outdated, but the current reporting path still does not expose collection-level or selector diagnostics; lifecycle validation itself was previously declined.
items.recommendation: Add a shared preflight for project-targeting CLI commands: absent .specle/changes, .specle/archive, .agents, and .agents/skills are allowed, while present paths must be directories; retain command-specific existence requirements. Standalone schemas export and blueprint validation do not inspect the current project's state. Address invalid or unreadable selectors separately without synthetic change rows.
items.rationale: Use common project-target preflight validation to report invalid path types early, while allowing paths that do not exist yet and exempting standalone resource commands.

items.description: Concurrent update can replace an index after a scan with a stale index.
items.evidence: The inventory scan and final index replacement have no mutual exclusion or concurrency check.
items.analysis: The thread is outdated; the async implementation still has an interval between scanning and replacement.
items.recommendation: Decline concurrent-operation coordination for this change.
items.rationale: Concurrent index and update operations against the same installation are outside the scope of this change.

items.description: Unescaped tab and newline characters corrupt text report columns and rows.
items.evidence: _report_changes joins raw values using tab delimiters; the status schema accepts any non-empty string.
items.analysis: Invalid names will be excluded under the separate accepted decision. Status values are currently open-ended in the JSON Schema and validated separately against lifecycle metadata; dependencies and diagnostics remain separate sources of text values.
items.recommendation: Defer status and kind enum consolidation to the separately defined consolidate-state-enums change; leave delivery events and other JSON keys out of scope.
items.rationale: The status and kind enum refactor is independent follow-up work, tracked by the explicitly defined consolidate-state-enums change; event values are not included.

items.description: CSV records use LF rather than RFC 4180 CRLF separators.
items.evidence: csv.writer is explicitly configured with lineterminator='\n'; the change requirements call for RFC 4180-compatible CSV.
items.analysis: Strict RFC 4180 consumers expect CRLF record separators. Existing LF-specific tests must be updated along with the writer.
items.recommendation: Emit CRLF record separators for CSV and update the affected behavioural tests.
items.rationale: Use CRLF for RFC 4180 compatibility despite a general preference for LF.

items.description: A selected defined change is reported with next action activate.
items.evidence: next_lifecycle_action maps defined to activate even when the selected record is already active.
items.analysis: Activation automatically runs the preparation chain, but the list can observe a selected change before that chain finishes. The next action depends on kind and existing preparation artifacts, not just the recorded status.
items.recommendation: For an unselected defined normal change or spike, report activate. For selected normal work, derive estimate, design when required by the estimate, tasks, or build from the preparation artifacts; for other kinds use their owning workflow.
items.rationale: A selected change should report the next applicable step in its actual preparation chain, taking existing artifacts and kind into account.

items.description: Selected S-sized estimated changes are reported with next action design.
items.evidence: next_lifecycle_action maps every estimated status to design without reading the estimate.
items.analysis: The lifecycle table directs S-sized work to tasks, but activation, estimate, and tasks currently require a design for all normal changes.
items.recommendation: For S-sized normal changes, skip design and proceed to tasks; align lifecycle policy, preparation skills, lifecycle metadata and the displayed next action with the recorded estimate.
items.rationale: S-sized changes should proceed from estimate to tasks without a design stage.

items.description: Nonterminal archive records may be assigned an archived completion date.
items.evidence: _report_timestamp uses archived_at for all archive statuses other than cancelled.
items.analysis: The listing intentionally exposes lifecycle-invalid records, but using a terminal date for a nonterminal record may mislead. Both terminal dates are optional.
items.recommendation: Use archived_at only for complete records and cancelled_at only for cancelled records; present an empty date for nonterminal records and whenever the applicable optional timestamp is missing or invalid.
items.rationale: Archive dates are optional and missing or invalid terminal timestamps must display as empty values.

items.description: A building change with completed tasks is reported with next action build.
items.evidence: next_lifecycle_action maps normal building to build without task completion context.
items.analysis: The build workflow directs work with no unfinished tasks to verify. A reusable change record can load and interpret the task plan on demand without treating task boxes as proof of verification.
items.recommendation: Defer artifact-aware next-action derivation to the separately defined refactor-change-record change.
items.rationale: The user chose a reusable lazy-loaded change record and cache, with a next-action method, as independent follow-up work.

items.description: The index regeneration test only checks that groups are nonempty.
items.evidence: test_index_regenerates_only_the_installed_index checks the groups field for truthiness.
items.analysis: That assertion cannot detect an index containing wrong managed skills; a behavioural comparison would tighten coverage.
items.recommendation: Add a focused behavioural assertion that regenerated index metadata reflects the installed managed skill, including a valid local metadata edit.
items.rationale: Regeneration should reflect the installed inventory, including valid user edits, and the test should detect incorrect index content.

items.description: CSV tests assume LF record separators.
items.evidence: CSV assertions in tests/test_main.py compare LF-only output.
items.analysis: Updating these assertions is part of the accepted CRLF output correction.
items.recommendation: Consolidate with the accepted CSV separator finding.
items.rationale: The same accepted CRLF change includes updating its affected tests.

items.description: `specle index` can overwrite the generated index when the required managed `specle` skill is absent or invalid.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:403-425 checks lifecycle diagnostics but does not require a valid discovered skill named `specle`; scan_managed_inventory exposes discovered managed metadata for that check.
items.analysis: The installed target has no separate expected-inventory baseline, so other managed skills must be accepted as installed. A valid managed `specle` skill is the sole necessary completeness condition: it owns the generated index location and identifies the installation as a Specle skill deployment. If that skill is absent or invalid while its index directory remains, the command can replace the existing index from an invalid inventory.
items.recommendation: Require a valid discovered managed `specle` skill before creating the temporary file, preserving the existing index otherwise; add a focused preservation test.
items.rationale: Require only the valid managed `specle` skill. Do not impose an ungrounded full-inventory or policy-completeness baseline.

items.description: The human `changes` report prints raw Unix seconds instead of the required calendar date.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:381 emits row['timestamp'] directly; requirements.md:26 and :40 require YYYY-MM-DD dates for active and archived text output.
items.analysis: For example, an active record with created_at 1795326755 is shown as `1795326755`, so both active creation and archive completion reports fail the documented human-facing date contract. JSON may retain durable Unix seconds; this affects only the text presentation.
items.recommendation: Format the validated durable timestamp as a deterministic YYYY-MM-DD value in text output, and cover active and archived text rows.
items.rationale: Correct the text dates and add clear headers. Extend the current change with an explicit `--csv` format that emits headered CSV, rather than relying on implicit tab-separated rows.

items.description: The next-action mapping omits the active `spiking` lifecycle state.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:387-398 has no `spiking` entry, while .agents/policies/lifecycle.md identifies `spiking` with next action `spike`.
items.analysis: A valid active spike is reported with the no-action placeholder despite having a required next workflow action. That makes the report inconsistent with the lifecycle policy and violates requirement 3.3.
items.recommendation: Derive or centralise the status-to-action mapping so the report includes `spiking -> spike` and remains aligned with lifecycle policy; add focused coverage.
items.rationale: The displayed next action must reflect the documented lifecycle state.

items.description: `specle changes` does not reject records that fail runtime lifecycle validation.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-1; independently confirmed: src/specle/main.py calls read_change_state without validate_runtime_records.
items.analysis: The shared reader enforces schema shape but not lifecycle evidence, terminal location, or concurrent-sidecar invariants. The requirement explicitly requires lifecycle diagnostics to produce non-zero output, so this is a functional gap.
items.recommendation: Validate the same buffered state against the managed lifecycle metadata before rendering, then report diagnostics without partial output.
items.rationale: `changes` is an observational schema-valid listing, not a lifecycle-validation command. Invalid lifecycle state should remain inspectable in the listing rather than being rejected.

items.description: Archive listing rejects valid cancelled changes because it always requires `archived_at`.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-2; independently confirmed: cancellation archives terminal records with `cancelled_at`, while src/specle/main.py reads only `archived_at` for every archive row.
items.analysis: The lifecycle policy permits archived `cancelled` records without `archived_at`, and both terminal timestamps are optional durable metadata. A single valid cancellation therefore prevents every archive format from listing any archive records under the current implementation.
items.recommendation: Use `archived_at` for completed records and `cancelled_at` for cancelled records when present. Treat either absent optional value as an empty human placeholder or null structured timestamp, not a diagnostic.
items.rationale: Every valid terminal archive must remain listable. Use the applicable terminal timestamp when available, but preserve the established optionality of both archived_at and cancelled_at.

items.description: The status-only next-action mapping can direct non-selected or abbreviated work to invalid workflows.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-3; independently confirmed against .agents/policies/lifecycle.md and the activate, bugfix, and refactor skills.
items.analysis: The displayed action depends on record kind and whether a normal change is selected, not solely on status. For example, an unselected planned normal change must be activated, and an abbreviated planned record belongs to its named bugfix or refactor workflow.
items.recommendation: Resolve actions from a record plus selection context in package-owned lifecycle code, with focused behaviour coverage; do not adopt the reviewer's broader metadata-driven redesign unless it proves necessary.
items.rationale: The displayed action must be valid for the record's kind and local selection context, not merely its status.

items.description: Invalid numeric timestamps can produce partial output or invalid JSON instead of one actionable diagnostic.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-4; independently confirmed: datetime conversion occurs during text/CSV output, and json.dumps permits NaN by default.
items.analysis: Schema-valid numeric floats can be non-finite or outside platform timestamp range. Text and CSV may emit their header before failing, while JSON can emit non-standard NaN. That contradicts the common invalid-state failure contract.
items.recommendation: Validate timestamp finiteness and UTC date conversion before choosing an output format; reject invalid values consistently and disallow non-finite JSON values. Use a portable CSV line terminator.
items.rationale: Malformed durable timestamps must fail consistently before producing partial or non-standard output.

items.description: Index regeneration replaces the index with restrictive temporary-file permissions and lacks several narrow output checks.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-5; independently confirmed: tempfile.mkstemp creates the replacement at mode 0600 and os.replace preserves it.
items.analysis: Regenerating an otherwise ordinary managed index changes its readability. The unqualified encoding and directory-destination handling are also weaker than the repository's existing staged-write pattern. The generated payload originates internally, so redundant schema validation needs separate justification.
items.recommendation: Preserve normal readable permissions, write UTF-8 explicitly, and provide an actionable directory-destination error. Keep the implementation focused; extracting it or revalidating the internally built payload is optional rather than required.
items.rationale: The index-only operation must not silently tighten ordinary generated-file readability and should report unsupported destinations clearly.

items.description: Several documented listing and index behaviours still lack direct focused coverage.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-6; independently confirmed from tests/test_main.py and the revised acceptance criteria.
items.analysis: The current tests cover representative formats and boundaries, but not active complete filtering, empty text/CSV results, ordering, dependency rendering, lifecycle diagnostics in every format, or all index replacement boundaries. The task plan also names files that were not needed.
items.recommendation: Add only focused behavioural cases that exercise the remaining acceptance criteria and align the completed task's file list with the implementation; do not add broad repeated workflow tests.
items.rationale: The remaining acceptance criteria need direct focused evidence; recurring workflow simulation remains out of scope.

items.description: The new synchronous CLI paths do not follow the repository's AnyIO convention, and README still says standalone index is deferred.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-changes-list.json: AGY-R2-7; independently confirmed in src/specle/main.py and README.md:43.
items.analysis: The parser argument placement is cosmetic, but synchronous filesystem scans and writes in async main are inconsistent with the repository convention. The README statement is now factually stale.
items.recommendation: Use the existing worker-thread pattern for filesystem operations and correct the deferred-command statement; do not change parser layout solely for aesthetics.
items.rationale: The README must not say that a delivered command is deferred. The async implementation concern is owned by the independent correct-to-thread-abuse bugfix.

items.description: An oversized integer timestamp raises before the report can emit its intended diagnostic.
items.evidence: src/specle/main.py:_report_timestamp calls math.isfinite(timestamp); `math.isfinite(10**400)` raises OverflowError before the guarded datetime conversion.
items.analysis: JSON supports arbitrary-size integers, and the state schema accepts them as numbers. An oversized epoch must follow the same actionable non-zero diagnostic contract as non-finite and platform-unrenderable timestamps, rather than producing a traceback.
items.recommendation: Guard the finiteness check itself against OverflowError and represent the record with its timestamp diagnostic without suppressing the rest of the collection.
items.rationale: Every unrenderable numeric timestamp must be shown with an actionable diagnostic; it must not abort or hide the remaining collection.

items.description: Schema-invalid records are currently hidden by the state reader or abort the entire listing rather than appearing with their error.
items.evidence: requirements.md requirement 3.2 and src/specle/change_state.py:_read_change_collection omit records whose status cannot be schema-validated; src/specle/main.py exits on any snapshot diagnostic.
items.analysis: A changes listing must not silently omit erroneous data or suppress the rest of the collection because one record is malformed. The user needs to see the named bad record and its diagnostic alongside valid records in every format.
items.recommendation: Revise the listing contract and reader boundary so each discoverable erroneous record is represented with an explicit diagnostic rather than skipped or causing a collection-wide abort; add focused output tests for malformed and schema-invalid records.
items.rationale: Expose erroneous records and their errors. Do not hide them or abort the entire listing merely because one record is invalid.
